items.title: Ellen Rowe interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 2, 2024
items.q: she did a portrait of Dudley Moore. And I painstakingly took that sucker down.

ctx.x: It’s very interesting how, you mentioned deep listening and how connected it is to technology. Because I was reading your bio and it reminded me of how I used to learn songs from records. So you know I want to learn the bass line first and there was this constant putting the needle down, getting a couple of measures, picking the needle up. I mean that was deep. Because you had no choice, it was deep.
Exactly. Yeah. I remember like cassette recordings I had of Marian McPartland when I was trying to transcribe her solo piano albums and you know it was push and rewind and © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

push and rewind and push and rewind. And you know the other beauty about that was that — one tape I remember in particular was running almost a half-step sharp and I transcribed a solo piece for — it was, she used to do these portraits of her guests sometimes on the Piano Jazz show. And she did a portrait of Dudley Moore. And I painstakingly took that sucker down. I could not believe she had played in C sharp minor but you know she was Marian, she could play in any key.
